targetName: Warm Paper Atelier Desk Mat Continuous Pad

terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: Direct inspection shows one thin padded mat with a broad rounded plan, continuous top field, compressed attached binding, inset low-contrast stitch path, and fine woven response. The unseen underside is conservatively inferred as a thin support; no manufacturing-grade dimensions are claimed.

reasoning: The outer silhouette is simple, but the reference identity depends on a continuous thin pad profile rather than the current raised inner tray.
The segmented stitches form one dense curve-following repetition system around four straight runs and four broad corners.
The main view and two low-angle insets expose separate macro crown, meso binding compression, and micro fiber/roughness response.
The hidden underside and exact thickness are inferred conservatively and judged through grounded contact rather than claimed as source fact.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Moderate depth covers the simple mass while requiring explicit continuous surface, attached binding, repeated stitches, three-frequency cloth response, stable contact, and unchanged runtime interaction anchors.

detailInventory.note: Eight reference-observed or explicitly inferred details map to implementation components/material overrides; hidden underside dimensions remain an inference.

details.description: Four broad plan corners remain independent of the mat's small vertical thickness.
The top is one nearly planar padded field with a restrained crown and no recessed tray gap.
A darker wrapped binding overlaps the side edge and reads as compressed upholstery rather than a floating circular tube.
details.scale: meso; about 0.11 world units wide and 0.07 high
details.affects: perimeter profile, attachment, and edge highlight

details.description: A shallow compressed channel carries the stitches just inside the binding without separating the top into another island.
details.scale: micro; channel width about 0.025 world units
details.affects: edge construction line and contact AO

details.description: Short low-contrast thread dashes repeat at stable arc-length spacing and follow the path tangent through all corners.
details.scale: micro; 0.075 world-unit dashes with visible gaps
details.affects: instanced repeated geometry and thread contrast

details.description: Fine interlaced fibers create dense directional crosshatch without a distant checkerboard pattern.
details.scale: micro; high-frequency weave above product-view pixel frequency
details.affects: independent height, roughness, AO, and neutral albedo channels

details.description: Broad low-contrast neutral tonal variation breaks uniformity without reading as dirt or owning the role color.
details.scale: macro and meso; irregular 0.12 to 0.45 mat-unit variation

details.description: The bound edge has lower bump amplitude and a restrained smoother crest highlight under grazing light.
details.scale: micro local response over the binding crest

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: The preserved 8.7 by 6.25 footprint reads as one broad, continuous, low-profile padded mat rather than a bumper surrounding a raised tray.
The attached binding, compressed stitch channel, and segmented stitches remain distinct in top and both low-angle reference views without floating or intersection.
Field and binding retain independently generated albedo, roughness, height, and AO responses with macro, meso, and micro frequency bands.
The visible model stays grounded while the approved topY, placement bounds, collider, sockets, and external hit surface remain unchanged.

featureGroups.name: Broad rounded plan and continuous low profile
qualityCriteria: The approved 8.7 by 6.25 footprint, z center, and 0.7 plan radius remain unchanged.
The top reads as one thin padded surface; no raised inner island or deep perimeter trough appears.
failureModes: corner radius is clamped by vertical thickness
mat reads as a tray, sharp slab, or thick cushion

featureGroups.name: Continuous surface, support, binding, and stitch structure
qualityCriteria: Surface, support layer, attached binding, stitch channel, and stitch system have explicit ownership under one root.
All visible layers derive from one rounded footprint so straight runs and corners remain registered.
failureModes: binding floats away from the surface or intersects it visibly
a separate field island recreates the current bumper-well structure

featureGroups.name: Compressed binding attachment and grounded contact
qualityCriteria: Binding attachment declares the surface edge socket, overlap/contact type, embed depth, and gap tolerance.
The support layer rests at the desk datum without a visible gap while the approved topY remains fixed.
failureModes: binding reads as a detached circular tube
mat floats above or clips into the desktop
visible geometry changes the external hit surface contract

featureGroups.name: Three-frequency woven field and compressed binding response
qualityCriteria: Field and binding define independent albedo, roughness, height, and AO responses without channel aliasing.
Neutral macro mottling, meso yarn variation, and micro crosshatch remain distinct under neutral and grazing light.
Binding uses lower bump amplitude and a localized smoother crest while preserving editable role colors.
failureModes: surface reads as flat plastic, stone noise, or a distant checkerboard
binding response is identical to the field and loses compressed-edge character

featureGroups.name: Reference viewpoints and interaction-preserving look-development
qualityCriteria: Top, left-front grazing, right-front grazing, desktop product, and mobile product views show the same registered geometry.
Neutral and grazing review proves relief survives relighting rather than being painted into albedo.
Current role colors stay editable and the unchanged collider/hit bounds remain aligned with the visible footprint.
failureModes: only an isolated top view passes while either low-angle edge view fails
review lighting hides attachment or contact artifacts
visible footprint diverges from the approved interaction boundary

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.

mustMatch: continuous low-profile rounded silhouette with no recessed tray
compressed binding attachment and stitch-channel registration
independent cloth PBR response at or above 0.7 extraction confidence
unchanged topY, collider, placement bounds, and external hit surface

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.

Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

coordinateFrame.scaleReference: Three.js world units; preserve 8.7 width, 6.25 depth, and world topY 0.11

shaderNotes: Prefer MeshPhysicalMaterial when clearcoat, sheen, transmission, or thin-surface response is observed; otherwise use MeshStandardMaterial-compatible PBR channels.

Use normal/bump/displacement only when they map to observed surface relief.
Use displacement geometry when the observed relief changes the close-up silhouette; texture-only relief is insufficient there.

ambientOcclusion.notes: Concentrate at binding overlap and stitch channel.

buildPasses.goal: Match material color, roughness, bump, and local variation.
acceptance: Reference-derived albedo palette records dominant, secondary, and accent colors per visible material.
Each important material defines roughness variation and at least one normal/bump/displacement response.
Local material overrides, dirt/wear/stains/moss/chips/scratches or equivalent masks are tied to evidenceRefs.

Generated preview uses independent PBR maps at 1024px or higher for the quality-first tier.
If source pixels are available, referencePbr extraction passed at confidence >= 0.7 or the pass is stopped/requesting better references.
Macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands are visible at the intended review distance without obvious tiling.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Add procedural surface locality such as normal/bump/displacement, AO, dirt, stains, chips, grain, moss, scratches, and wear.
acceptance: Every required material feature group has local overrides or surfaceDetail tied to evidenceRefs.

AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make material and form readable under neutral turntable lighting plus optional reference lighting.
acceptance: lightingFromPhoto identifies key light direction/color/intensity, fill light, rim or environment light, and ambient color.
Exposure, tone mapping, background color/gradient, shadow softness, and contact shadow behavior are specified.
Lighting does not hide geometry/material gaps and screenshots can be compared fairly to the reference.
Neutral, grazing, and reference-matched lighting checks distinguish material errors from lighting errors.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make the model ready for future animation, transformation, physics, or destruction.
acceptance: Macro and movable meso components have stable pivot nodes.
Sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata are present for future runtime actions.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Protect runtime performance after visual fidelity is accepted.
acceptance: Triangle count, draw calls, instancing, LOD strategy, and FPS target are documented or verified.
Repeated detail is instanced or simplified where possible without breaking silhouette/material believability.
